description: Layer map for tools/architecture/include_layers.py. Lower rank = more stable; an include from a lower-rank source into a higher-rank header is an upward include. Layer membership is DERIVED from the component manifest named by source_of_truth: a file owned by an extracted (non-legacy) component takes the layer of its family, and a contract header takes the contract layer. Hand-written entries survive only in monolith_overrides, and only for paths still inside the sakura_app monolith. Run 'include_layers.py check-derivation' to prove the overrides still agree with the manifest.

rules: Classification order: (1) contract headers - every public_header of every component plus everything under contract_prefixes - become contract_layer; (2) a file listed in a non-legacy component's sources or private_headers takes the layer of that component's family; (3) a file left over inside the sakura_app monolith takes the longest-matching monolith_overrides prefix; (4) anything else is reported as unclassified and counted, never silently dropped.
family shared-state = rank 0: sakura_shareddata_contract ships no translation unit at all, only the SharedData ABI headers, so it is a pure contract with nothing below it.

family platform-primitives = rank 2 (L2-platform): uri/serialization/security/storage/filesystem/request wrap OS and file-format primitives for every process; they sit above the string/memory foundation and below any document concept.

family authority-process-platform = rank 2 (L2-platform): the control-IPC protocol, security, transport and endpoint components are the cross-process plumbing of the control process, peers of the other platform primitives (controlipc_transport depends only on controlipc_security/protocol and sakura_security).

family terminal-harness = rank 2 (L2-platform): the tmux core, harness bridge, harness CLI and terminal tools are a self-contained automation subsystem that already lives under sakura_core/platform/harnessbridge; nothing in it depends on the document or workbench model, and the monolith depends on it (sakura_app -> sakura_terminal_cli), so it belongs below the domain layers.

family document-editor = rank 3 (L3-workbench-model): SelectionSession, EditorFrameEvents and DocumentSession are the extracted editor domain model, exactly the layer the sakura_core/workbench tree already occupied.
family win32-adapters = rank 4 (L4-legacy-ui): Win32EditorFrameAdapter binds the editor frame contract to HWND-level Win32 UI, the same layer as the rest of sakura_core/window.
family process-lifecycle = rank 5 (L5-composition): EditorAppLifecycle sequences editor process startup and shutdown from sakura_core/_main, i.e. it is part of the composition root.

family legacy = rank 5 (L5-composition) for manifest edge direction only: sakura_app is the monolithic executable that composes every extracted component. Its individual files are NOT classified by this rank - they go through monolith_overrides.
family legacy-language-resources = rank 4 (L4-legacy-ui): sakura_lang ships localized dialog/menu resources, a UI-layer artifact (its .rc files are outside the C++ include scan).
every *-tests family = rank 6 (L6-tests): a test binary may depend on anything, so it is the topmost layer and can never produce an upward edge (its sources live outside the scanned source roots).
When several layers share a rank, the one marked derived_target receives family-derived files; the other exists only as an override target.

monolith_overrides prefixes nest on purpose and the longest prefix wins, exactly like the pre-derivation map. Two overrides with the SAME prefix and different layers are an error; a nested prefix is not.

monolith_overrides.reason: The precompiled header every monolith translation unit must include; it is foundation by construction, not by ownership.
monolith_overrides.removal_condition: Remove when sakura_app no longer uses a repository-wide precompiled header, or when a sakura_foundation component owns it in modules.json.
